page: UpCloud PREMIUM-80xCPU-512GB is a premium-class virtual server configured with 80 vCPUs and 512.0 GB of RAM, running on the KVM hypervisor. The system is powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It features 80 physical cores with a single thread per core and a shared CPU allocation. The processor cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. The server includes a bundled 500 GB local SSD and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier CPU and memory performance. The server achieves top 10% placement in multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng, Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, and PassMark CPU metrics. It demonstrates strong capabilities in cryptographic and compression tasks, with single-threaded gzip compression reaching 39.97 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 813.68 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth for small cached blocks is exceptionally high at 9301.72 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write speeds remain strong at 262.5 GB/sec and 125.96 GB/sec respectively. Redis SET operations perform in the top tier at 124.66 million operations per second.

Despite the high-density compute and memory allocation, certain performance tradeoffs exist. While prompt processing for small and medium LLM models falls in the average tier, text generation speeds are weak, registering at 46.51 tokens per second for small models and 7.85 tokens per second for medium models. Additionally, the CPU allocation is shared, which may introduce performance variability under sustained multi-tenant load. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a dense consolidation of high-core-count AMD EPYC processing and substantial memory, making it highly resource-efficient for parallelized workloads that do not require dedicated CPU pinning. This server configuration is highly suited for heavy multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving.
